reason: E1 supports the unification of static lattice distortion and temperature via an effective temperature, but does not address electronegativity-driven chemical fluctuations or their role in stabilizing phases against separation. E2 shows electronegativity differences contribute to local chemical fluctuation and lattice distortion in thermoelectric materials, but does not link this to phase stability or an energetic barrier against ordering. The key mechanistic premise that enhanced distortion raises a barrier to phase separation is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Static bond length variations (atomic radii mismatches) and local chemical fluctuations (electronegativity differences) combine to produce local lattice distortion in multi-metal solid solutions.
Lattice distortion from atomic size mismatch and temperature fluctuations can be unified through an effective temperature scaling law in high-entropy alloys.
Electronegativity differences contribute to local chemical fluctuation and can induce large lattice distortion in high-entropy thermoelectric materials.
Enhanced lattice distortion raises an energetic barrier for phase separation or ordering, suppressing detrimental atomic rearrangements.
Greater lattice distortion stabilizes a single-phase solid solution over a broad temperature range up to 1923 K.
